merges.englishGloss: Needle lace edging on a headscarf or handkerchief
merges.reason: Both sets show needle-made lace borders. Floral versus triangular edging and caption versus close view remain in the same conservative group.

merges.englishGloss: Raised metallic floral or branch embroidery on clothing
merges.reason: Metallic raised botanical ornament is the shared visual motif across the traditional dress and the other embroidered accessories.

merges.englishGloss: An upright hot-drink urn with a dispensing tap
merges.reason: The salep vessel and samovar share the essential tall heated-vessel-and-tap composition. Drink identity and accessory type do not split this motif.

merges.englishGloss: Visible fabric repair with patches or reinforcing hand stitches
merges.reason: Both groups visibly strengthen a worn clothing area. Body location and repair material are consolidated conservatively.

merges.englishGloss: Halved stone fruit displaying a large oval pit or pit cavity
merges.reason: Apricot versus plum, accessory type and incidental colour do not split the shared cut-fruit composition.

merges.englishGloss: Hand-dyed textiles shown during dyeing or beside the dye source
merges.reason: Yarn versus cloth and dye ingredients do not create independent hand-dyeing scenarios. Process and sample views are kept in one conservative group.

merges.englishGloss: Paired serrated herb leaves arranged along a stem
merges.reason: Nettle and mint share this specific opposing toothed-leaf composition. Plant names and accessory surfaces do not split the visual motif.

merges.englishGloss: A voluminous garment tube gathered into a narrow cuff
merges.reason: Sleeve versus trouser placement does not split the same narrow-cuff gathering motif.

botanicalRevisionReason: Four complete items about linden flower clusters with a distinctive long bract replace the fuzzy oval herb-leaf group. This gives more structural headroom around the conservatively merged mint/nettle motif.
